title: Down a Row is Ten More

steps.body: Move down one row and you add ten. 34 is above 44. Ten more than 34 is 44.
steps.narration: Move down one row and you add ten. Thirty-four is above forty-four. Ten more than thirty-four is forty-four.

widget.prompt: Going down a row adds 10. Start at 34 and make one hop of 10. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: That's just one more (one spot right). Down a whole row adds TEN: 44.
That's two rows down (twenty more). One row down from 34 is 44.

widget.successFeedback: 34 down one row is 44 — ten more!

predict.prompt: One hop of 10 from 34 — which digit of the number will change?
predict.reveal: A ten-hop moves you a whole row: the tens digit climbs by one and the ones digit stays exactly where it was.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents chart pattern.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for chart pattern must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines chart pattern.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: The number below 34 on the chart is 44.

widget.prompt: What is ten more than 34 (one row down)?

commonErrors.feedback: 35 is one MORE (right). Ten more (down a row) is 44.
24 is ten LESS (up a row). Ten MORE is 44.

steps.body: Up a row takes ten away. A whole column shares the same ones digit: 4, 14, 24, 34.
steps.narration: Up a row takes ten away. A whole column shares the same ones digit: four, fourteen, twenty-four, thirty-four.

steps.body: Match each number to ten more.

widget.prompt: Match each number to the one just below it (ten more).

pairErrors.feedback: 34 plus ten is 44, not 68. Add just one ten.
58 plus ten is 68. 44 is ten more than 34.

widget.successFeedback: Each number met the one below it — ten more each time!

commonErrors.feedback: 59 is one more. Ten more than 58 is 68.
48 is ten LESS. Ten MORE than 58 is 68.

explanationVariants: A column runs straight down, and every number in it shares the same ones digit.
Down a column only the tens change, so the ones digit stays the same.

widget.prompt: What do all the numbers in one column share?

options.label: the same ones digit
options.feedback: Yes — a column is 4, 14, 24, 34… only the tens change.

options.label: the same tens digit
options.feedback: Same tens digit means the same ROW, not a column. A column shares the ones digit.

options.label: nothing
options.feedback: A column has a strong pattern: every number ends in the same ones digit.

explanationVariants: Each row down adds ten, so two rows down adds twenty: 27 + 20 = 47.

widget.prompt: Go down two rows from 27 (add ten twice). What number?

commonErrors.feedback: 37 is only ONE row down. Two rows adds ten twice: 47.
That added two ONES. Two rows down adds two TENS: 27 + 20 = 47.

hints: Each row down is ten more.

takeaways: A column shares the ones digit.
steps.teaser: next chapter: reading and writing numerals to 120.

concept.body: Slow it down. One row down is ten more. Below 12 is 22. Below 22 is 32. The ones stay the same.
concept.narration: One row down is ten more. Below twelve is twenty-two. Below twenty-two is thirty-two. The ones stay the same.

explanationVariants: Ten more than 12 is 22 (one row down).

commonErrors.feedback: 13 is one more. Ten more than 12 is 22.
2 is ten LESS. Ten MORE than 12 is 22.
